title: Macroeconomics II
topics: Money, credit and the financial system
The multiplier in an open economy

items.q: Open-economy multiplier may be defined as
o: the magnifier of spending when part of each extra naira leaks into purchases from abroad
the requirement that combined import and export responsiveness exceed one before a weaker currency narrows the trade gap
the change in outlay that follows a change in the worth of the assets people hold
the set of income and interest combinations at which spending plans and output are equal
items.s: Open-economy multiplier: the magnifier of spending when part of each extra naira leaks into purchases from abroad. The other options describe Wealth effect, Marshall-Lerner condition, IS schedule.
items.t: The multiplier in an open economy

items.q: The statement “the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch” describes which of the following?
o: NAIRU
Shoe-leather cost
Sacrifice ratio
Natural rate of unemployment
items.s: Natural rate of unemployment is the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Shoe-leather cost?
o: the total that firms will offer at each price level while some costs are held by past bargains
large purchases of assets by the central authority to push cash into the system when interest cannot fall further
the effort and time used up in holding less cash when prices are rising quickly
the division of taxing and spending powers among levels of government
items.s: Shoe-leather cost: the effort and time used up in holding less cash when prices are rising quickly. The other options describe Short-run aggregate supply, Fiscal federalism, Quantitative easing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Quantitative easing.
o: the loss of purchasing power that holders of cash suffer when the state prints money
the tendency for poorer economies to grow faster and close the gap with richer ones
large purchases of assets by the central authority to push cash into the system when interest cannot fall further
holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt
items.s: Quantitative easing: large purchases of assets by the central authority to push cash into the system when interest cannot fall further. The other options describe Inflation tax, Precautionary motive, Convergence.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Capital flight?
o: the rapid movement of funds abroad when holders lose confidence
the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal
a rise in a currency's value against others under market forces
the rise in the amount of equipment each worker has to work with
items.s: Capital flight: the rapid movement of funds abroad when holders lose confidence. The other options describe Appreciation, Hysteresis, Capital deepening.

items.q: Surplus labour view may be defined as
o: the tendency for poorer economies to grow faster and close the gap with richer ones
the rise in prices that households expect, which inclines them to spend sooner and set aside less
the idea that extra farm hands can move into factories without any fall in harvests
the number of times a unit of currency changes hands in financing a year's output
items.s: Surplus labour view: the idea that extra farm hands can move into factories without any fall in harvests. The other options describe Inflationary expectations, Convergence, Velocity of circulation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Deflationary spiral?
o: the proposition that a change in the stock of cash brings a proportionate change in prices when output is fixed
the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal
a fall in prices and spending that feeds on itself as buyers delay purchases
the loss of output needed to bring a rise in prices down by a given amount
items.s: Deflationary spiral: a fall in prices and spending that feeds on itself as buyers delay purchases. The other options describe Hysteresis, Quantity theory, Sacrifice ratio.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Natural rate of unemployment?
o: the rise in the amount of equipment each worker has to work with
the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch
the proportion of adults who are either in work or actively seeking it
pay set above the going level to encourage effort and reduce quitting
items.s: Natural rate of unemployment: the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch. The other options describe Participation share, Efficiency wage, Capital deepening.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Primary balance?
o: the gap between receipts and outlay before interest on past borrowing is counted
the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high
the revenue a government gains by issuing currency that costs little to produce
the shortfall of spending that leaves output below its full-employment level
items.s: Primary balance: the gap between receipts and outlay before interest on past borrowing is counted. The other options describe Recessionary gap, Seigniorage, Real wage rigidity.

items.q: Exchange rate targeting may be defined as
o: the expense of changing listed charges when prices move
a sudden change in the cost or availability of inputs that shifts what firms will offer at every price
the result that an equal rise in public outlay and in taxes still leaves income higher
fixing or limiting the value of the currency against another as the anchor of policy
items.s: Exchange rate targeting: fixing or limiting the value of the currency against another as the anchor of policy. The other options describe Supply shock, Balanced-budget multiplier, Menu cost.

items.q: Quantity theory may be defined as
o: the proposition that a change in the stock of cash brings a proportionate change in prices when output is fixed
the idea that a rise in output calls forth a larger proportional rise in outlay on new plant
the view that currencies should exchange so that a basket of items costs the same everywhere
the claim that borrowing now means higher taxes later, so private spending does not change
items.s: Quantity theory: the proposition that a change in the stock of cash brings a proportionate change in prices when output is fixed. The other options describe Accelerator, Ricardian equivalence, Purchasing power parity.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Real wage rigidity may be defined as
o: the view that expansion springs from within the economy through knowledge and skills rather than from outside
a rise in the general price level that people foresaw and allowed for in their bargains
the condition in which a state can keep meeting its obligations without endlessly borrowing more
the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high
items.s: Real wage rigidity: the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high. The other options describe Debt sustainability, Endogenous growth, Anticipated inflation.

items.q: The statement “holding cash because receipts and payments are not perfectly timed” describes which of the following?
o: Seigniorage
High-powered money
Transactions motive
Financial intermediation
items.s: Transactions motive is holding cash because receipts and payments are not perfectly timed.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Appreciation.
o: the chain by which a change in the policy interest works through credit and the currency to spending
pay set above the going level to encourage effort and reduce quitting
a rise in a currency's value against others under market forces
the work of banks in taking funds from savers and lending them to borrowers
items.s: Appreciation: a rise in a currency's value against others under market forces. The other options describe Transmission mechanism, Financial intermediation, Efficiency wage.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Structural deficit?
o: the rise in the amount of equipment each worker has to work with
a framework in which the central authority announces a price goal and is judged on reaching it
a deliberate lowering of a currency's fixed value against others
the shortfall that would remain if the economy were already at full employment
items.s: Structural deficit: the shortfall that would remain if the economy were already at full employment. The other options describe Inflation targeting, Devaluation, Capital deepening.

items.q: Which term is described by “the interest a central authority charges when it lends to banks overnight”?
o: Moral suasion
Credit ceiling
Exchange rate targeting
Policy rate
items.s: Policy rate is the interest a central authority charges when it lends to banks overnight.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Okun's law?
o: the observed tendency for each extra point of joblessness to be matched by a fall in output relative to capacity
spending that rises and falls with income, as household consumption does
the share of each extra naira of income that is spent on items from abroad
the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch
items.s: Okun's law: the observed tendency for each extra point of joblessness to be matched by a fall in output relative to capacity. The other options describe Induced expenditure, Natural rate of unemployment, Marginal propensity to import.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Efficiency wage?
o: pay set above the going level to encourage effort and reduce quitting
the number by which an initial change in spending is magnified into a larger change in income
the lift to private spending that public outlay can give when it improves conditions for business
the part of a shortfall caused by weak activity rather than by deliberate choices
items.s: Efficiency wage: pay set above the going level to encourage effort and reduce quitting. The other options describe Crowding-in, Expenditure multiplier, Cyclical deficit.

items.q: The statement “the condition that returns on similar assets are equal across countries once expected currency moves are allowed for” describes which of the following?
o: Marshall-Lerner condition
Interest rate parity
Devaluation
Purchasing power parity
items.s: Interest rate parity is the condition that returns on similar assets are equal across countries once expected currency moves are allowed for.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Autonomous expenditure?
o: spending that does not depend on the level of income in the period
the set of income and interest combinations at which the wish to hold cash equals the amount in circulation
a rise in the general price level that people foresaw and allowed for in their bargains
the pattern in which a weaker currency worsens the trade gap before improving it
items.s: Autonomous expenditure: spending that does not depend on the level of income in the period. The other options describe LM schedule, J-curve, Anticipated inflation.
items.t: The multiplier in an open economy

items.q: Which term is described by “the rapid movement of funds abroad when holders lose confidence”?
o: Foreign reserves
Interest rate parity
Capital flight
Marshall-Lerner condition
items.s: Capital flight is the rapid movement of funds abroad when holders lose confidence.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Okun's law.
o: the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high
the practice of refusing loans to some applicants at the going interest instead of raising the charge
the observed tendency for each extra point of joblessness to be matched by a fall in output relative to capacity
a deliberate lowering of a currency's fixed value against others
items.s: Okun's law: the observed tendency for each extra point of joblessness to be matched by a fall in output relative to capacity. The other options describe Devaluation, Credit rationing, Real wage rigidity.

items.q: The statement “the surplus a firm thinks a project will bring, which governs whether it goes ahead” describes which of the following?
o: Permanent income view
Life-cycle view of saving
Expected profitability
Wealth effect
items.s: Expected profitability is the surplus a firm thinks a project will bring, which governs whether it goes ahead.

items.q: The statement “the shortfall of spending that leaves output below its full-employment level” describes which of the following?
o: Short-run aggregate supply
Supply shock
Recessionary gap
Aggregate demand
items.s: Recessionary gap is the shortfall of spending that leaves output below its full-employment level.

items.q: The statement “deliberate changes in taxing or spending made to steer the economy” describes which of the following?
o: Debt monetisation
Cyclical deficit
Structural deficit
Discretionary fiscal policy
items.s: Discretionary fiscal policy is deliberate changes in taxing or spending made to steer the economy.

items.q: The statement “pay set above the going level to encourage effort and reduce quitting” describes which of the following?
o: Okun's law
Insider-outsider
Efficiency wage
Participation share
items.s: Efficiency wage is pay set above the going level to encourage effort and reduce quitting.

items.q: All of the following belong to Fiscal policy and public finance EXCEPT
o: Structural deficit
J-curve
Cyclical deficit
Discretionary fiscal policy
items.s: Every other option belongs to Fiscal policy and public finance. “J-curve” belongs to The open economy, not Fiscal policy and public finance.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Liquidity trap?
o: a position where adding to the stock of cash no longer lowers interest because holders keep any extra idle
the lift to private spending that public outlay can give when it improves conditions for business
the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal
the time and effort spent looking for a suitable opening
items.s: Liquidity trap: a position where adding to the stock of cash no longer lowers interest because holders keep any extra idle. The other options describe Hysteresis, Job search, Crowding-in.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Inflationary expectations.
o: the rise in prices that households expect, which inclines them to spend sooner and set aside less
the difference between what the economy actually produces and what it could produce with its resources fully used
the idea that extra farm hands can move into factories without any fall in harvests
the idea that people smooth their outlay across a lifetime, borrowing when young and drawing down when old
items.s: Inflationary expectations: the rise in prices that households expect, which inclines them to spend sooner and set aside less. The other options describe Output gap, Life-cycle view of saving, Surplus labour view.

items.q: Which term is described by “the surplus a firm thinks a project will bring, which governs whether it goes ahead”?
o: Expected profitability
User cost of capital
Relative income view
Wealth effect
items.s: Expected profitability is the surplus a firm thinks a project will bring, which governs whether it goes ahead.

items.q: Permanent income view may be defined as
o: the idea that outlay rests on the means people expect to keep over the long term rather than this year's figure
the ratio of the change in income to the change in tax collection that brought it about
the share of each extra naira of income that is spent on items from abroad
a rise in a currency's value against others under market forces
items.s: Permanent income view: the idea that outlay rests on the means people expect to keep over the long term rather than this year's figure. The other options describe Tax multiplier, Appreciation, Marginal propensity to import.

items.q: The statement “the idea that outlay rests on the means people expect to keep over the long term rather than this year's figure” describes which of the following?
o: Expected profitability
Permanent income view
Accelerator
Inflationary expectations
items.s: Permanent income view is the idea that outlay rests on the means people expect to keep over the long term rather than this year's figure.

items.q: High-powered money may be defined as
o: the notes and coin held by the public plus the reserves banks keep with the central authority
holding cash because receipts and payments are not perfectly timed
the observed tendency for each extra point of joblessness to be matched by a fall in output relative to capacity
the lift to private spending that public outlay can give when it improves conditions for business
items.s: High-powered money: the notes and coin held by the public plus the reserves banks keep with the central authority. The other options describe Crowding-in, Transactions motive, Okun's law.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Okun's law may be defined as
o: the observed tendency for each extra point of joblessness to be matched by a fall in output relative to capacity
the total amount of finished output that buyers at home and abroad wish to purchase at each price level
a limit on how much banks may lend in total or to particular sectors
fixing or limiting the value of the currency against another as the anchor of policy
items.s: Okun's law: the observed tendency for each extra point of joblessness to be matched by a fall in output relative to capacity. The other options describe Aggregate demand, Exchange rate targeting, Credit ceiling.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Quantitative easing?
o: the part of output growth not explained by more labour and equipment, reflecting better methods
large purchases of assets by the central authority to push cash into the system when interest cannot fall further
spending that does not depend on the level of income in the period
the shortfall of spending that leaves output below its full-employment level
items.s: Quantitative easing: large purchases of assets by the central authority to push cash into the system when interest cannot fall further. The other options describe Autonomous expenditure, Total factor productivity, Recessionary gap.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Devaluation?
o: deliberate changes in taxing or spending made to steer the economy
the boost to spending when a fixed stock of cash buys more because prices have fallen
the practice of refusing loans to some applicants at the going interest instead of raising the charge
a deliberate lowering of a currency's fixed value against others
items.s: Devaluation: a deliberate lowering of a currency's fixed value against others. The other options describe Credit rationing, Real balance effect, Discretionary fiscal policy.

items.q: Participation share may be defined as
o: the divide between those already in work who bargain for pay and those outside who cannot
a fall in prices and spending that feeds on itself as buyers delay purchases
the gap between receipts and outlay before interest on past borrowing is counted
the proportion of adults who are either in work or actively seeking it
items.s: Participation share: the proportion of adults who are either in work or actively seeking it. The other options describe Insider-outsider, Primary balance, Deflationary spiral.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Relative income view?
o: the loss of purchasing power that holders of cash suffer when the state prints money
the idea that a household's outlay is set by how its means compare with those of people around it
the claim that borrowing now means higher taxes later, so private spending does not change
the total that firms will offer at each price level while some costs are held by past bargains
items.s: Relative income view: the idea that a household's outlay is set by how its means compare with those of people around it. The other options describe Inflation tax, Ricardian equivalence, Short-run aggregate supply.

items.q: Velocity of circulation may be defined as
o: the number of times a unit of currency changes hands in financing a year's output
the view that currencies should exchange so that a basket of items costs the same everywhere
the gain in output per head when a falling birth rate leaves more people at working age
the divide between those already in work who bargain for pay and those outside who cannot
items.s: Velocity of circulation: the number of times a unit of currency changes hands in financing a year's output. The other options describe Demographic dividend, Purchasing power parity, Insider-outsider.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Which of the following best describes Seigniorage?
o: the loss of output needed to bring a rise in prices down by a given amount
the revenue a government gains by issuing currency that costs little to produce
the idea that people smooth their outlay across a lifetime, borrowing when young and drawing down when old
the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal
items.s: Seigniorage: the revenue a government gains by issuing currency that costs little to produce. The other options describe Hysteresis, Sacrifice ratio, Life-cycle view of saving.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Which of the following best describes Efficiency wage?
o: pay set above the going level to encourage effort and reduce quitting
the total producible once all costs have adjusted, fixed by resources and methods rather than by prices
the loss of output needed to bring a rise in prices down by a given amount
the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch
items.s: Efficiency wage: pay set above the going level to encourage effort and reduce quitting. The other options describe Sacrifice ratio, Long-run aggregate supply, Natural rate of unemployment.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Deflationary spiral?
o: the share of deposits that banks must keep as balances with the central authority
the use of persuasion by the central authority instead of binding rule to steer lending
a fall in prices and spending that feeds on itself as buyers delay purchases
the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal
items.s: Deflationary spiral: a fall in prices and spending that feeds on itself as buyers delay purchases. The other options describe Moral suasion, Reserve requirement, Hysteresis.

items.q: The statement “the idea that people smooth their outlay across a lifetime, borrowing when young and drawing down when old” describes which of the following?
o: Permanent income view
Life-cycle view of saving
User cost of capital
Accelerator
items.s: Life-cycle view of saving is the idea that people smooth their outlay across a lifetime, borrowing when young and drawing down when old.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Induced expenditure?
o: the number by which an initial change in spending is magnified into a larger change in income
spending that rises and falls with income, as household consumption does
the shortfall that would remain if the economy were already at full employment
the total amount of finished output that buyers at home and abroad wish to purchase at each price level
items.s: Induced expenditure: spending that rises and falls with income, as household consumption does. The other options describe Structural deficit, Aggregate demand, Expenditure multiplier.
items.t: The multiplier in an open economy

items.q: Which term is described by “the number by which an initial change in spending is magnified into a larger change in income”?
o: Expenditure multiplier
Autonomous expenditure
Open-economy multiplier
Marginal propensity to import
items.s: Expenditure multiplier is the number by which an initial change in spending is magnified into a larger change in income.
items.t: The multiplier in an open economy

items.q: Which of the following best describes Shoe-leather cost?

the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch
the loss of purchasing power that holders of cash suffer when the state prints money
the effort and time used up in holding less cash when prices are rising quickly
items.s: Shoe-leather cost: the effort and time used up in holding less cash when prices are rising quickly. The other options describe Debt monetisation, Inflation tax, Natural rate of unemployment.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Hysteresis?
o: the condition that returns on similar assets are equal across countries once expected currency moves are allowed for
the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal
a limit on how much banks may lend in total or to particular sectors
the proportion of adults who are either in work or actively seeking it
items.s: Hysteresis: the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal. The other options describe Interest rate parity, Credit ceiling, Participation share.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Velocity of circulation.
o: the yearly expense of owning and running a machine, covering interest, wear and upkeep
the gain in output per head when a falling birth rate leaves more people at working age
a name for the jobless share below which price rises begin to accelerate
the number of times a unit of currency changes hands in financing a year's output
items.s: Velocity of circulation: the number of times a unit of currency changes hands in financing a year's output. The other options describe User cost of capital, NAIRU, Demographic dividend.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Anticipated inflation?

the loss of purchasing power that holders of cash suffer when the state prints money
a rise in the general price level that people foresaw and allowed for in their bargains
the ratio of the change in income to the change in tax collection that brought it about
items.s: Anticipated inflation: a rise in the general price level that people foresaw and allowed for in their bargains. The other options describe Inflation tax, Tax multiplier, Discretionary fiscal policy.

items.q: Capital flight may be defined as

a person who has stopped looking for work and so is no longer counted as jobless
the idea that extra farm hands can move into factories without any fall in harvests
the rapid movement of funds abroad when holders lose confidence
items.s: Capital flight: the rapid movement of funds abroad when holders lose confidence. The other options describe Surplus labour view, Discouraged worker, NAIRU.

the total producible once all costs have adjusted, fixed by resources and methods rather than by prices
holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt
the division of taxing and spending powers among levels of government

the difference between what the economy actually produces and what it could produce with its resources fully used
the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high
a name for the jobless share below which price rises begin to accelerate
items.s: Real wage rigidity: the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high. The other options describe NAIRU, Output gap, Inflation targeting.

items.q: Which term is described by “the total producible once all costs have adjusted, fixed by resources and methods rather than by prices”?
o: Recessionary gap
Short-run aggregate supply
Long-run aggregate supply
Output gap
items.s: Long-run aggregate supply is the total producible once all costs have adjusted, fixed by resources and methods rather than by prices.

the holdings of other countries' money and gold that a state uses to defend its currency
the use of persuasion by the central authority instead of binding rule to steer lending
the shortfall of spending that leaves output below its full-employment level

the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high
a position where adding to the stock of cash no longer lowers interest because holders keep any extra idle
the condition that returns on similar assets are equal across countries once expected currency moves are allowed for

the number of times a unit of currency changes hands in financing a year's output
the holdings of other countries' money and gold that a state uses to defend its currency
the practice of refusing loans to some applicants at the going interest instead of raising the charge

items.q: Which term is described by “holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt”?

Velocity of circulation
Precautionary motive
Money multiplier
items.s: Precautionary motive is holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt.

holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt
the combination of taxing, spending and interest measures used together
the view that currencies should exchange so that a basket of items costs the same everywhere
items.s: Purchasing power parity: the view that currencies should exchange so that a basket of items costs the same everywhere. The other options describe NAIRU, Precautionary motive, Policy mix.

the proposition that a change in the stock of cash brings a proportionate change in prices when output is fixed

Permanent income view
User cost of capital
Wealth effect

o: Job search
Participation share
Real wage rigidity
Insider-outsider

the total producible once all costs have adjusted, fixed by resources and methods rather than by prices
the set of income and interest combinations at which the wish to hold cash equals the amount in circulation
holding cash because receipts and payments are not perfectly timed

LM schedule

Quantity theory
Financial intermediation

the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch
the expense of changing listed charges when prices move
items.s: Natural rate of unemployment: the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch. The other options describe Hysteresis, Menu cost, Deflationary spiral.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the financing of a shortfall by creating money rather than by borrowing from the public”
o: Primary balance
Ricardian equivalence
Fiscal federalism
Debt monetisation
items.s: Debt monetisation is the financing of a shortfall by creating money rather than by borrowing from the public.

items.q: The correct meaning of Expenditure multiplier is
o: the number by which an initial change in spending is magnified into a larger change in income
the magnifier of spending when part of each extra naira leaks into purchases from abroad
the ratio of the change in income to the change in tax collection that brought it about
spending that does not depend on the level of income in the period
items.s: Expenditure multiplier: the number by which an initial change in spending is magnified into a larger change in income. The other options describe Tax multiplier, Open-economy multiplier, Autonomous expenditure.
items.t: The multiplier in an open economy

items.q: Money multiplier may be defined as
o: the ratio of total deposits banks can support to the reserves held behind them
holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt
the proposition that a change in the stock of cash brings a proportionate change in prices when output is fixed
holding cash because receipts and payments are not perfectly timed
items.s: Money multiplier: the ratio of total deposits banks can support to the reserves held behind them. The other options describe Transactions motive, Quantity theory, Precautionary motive.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: In this course, Steady state refers to
o: the position where the equipment per worker stops changing because new investment only replaces wear
the view that expansion springs from within the economy through knowledge and skills rather than from outside
the gain in output per head when a falling birth rate leaves more people at working age
the idea that extra farm hands can move into factories without any fall in harvests
items.s: Steady state: the position where the equipment per worker stops changing because new investment only replaces wear. The other options describe Demographic dividend, Endogenous growth, Surplus labour view.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Menu cost?
o: the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal
the expense of changing listed charges when prices move
a fall in prices and spending that feeds on itself as buyers delay purchases
the share of the workforce left jobless when the market for work is in balance, from search and mismatch
items.s: Menu cost: the expense of changing listed charges when prices move. The other options describe Deflationary spiral, Natural rate of unemployment, Hysteresis.

items.q: “the proposition that a change in the stock of cash brings a proportionate change in prices when output is fixed” is the definition of
o: Seigniorage
Quantity theory
Precautionary motive
Financial intermediation
items.s: Quantity theory is the proposition that a change in the stock of cash brings a proportionate change in prices when output is fixed.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Expected profitability?
o: the idea that people smooth their outlay across a lifetime, borrowing when young and drawing down when old
the surplus a firm thinks a project will bring, which governs whether it goes ahead
the rise in prices that households expect, which inclines them to spend sooner and set aside less
the idea that a household's outlay is set by how its means compare with those of people around it
items.s: Expected profitability: the surplus a firm thinks a project will bring, which governs whether it goes ahead. The other options describe Inflationary expectations, Relative income view, Life-cycle view of saving.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the idea that people smooth their outlay across a lifetime, borrowing when young and drawing down when old”
o: Expected profitability
Life-cycle view of saving
Permanent income view
Relative income view
items.s: Life-cycle view of saving is the idea that people smooth their outlay across a lifetime, borrowing when young and drawing down when old.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Velocity of circulation.
o: the work of banks in taking funds from savers and lending them to borrowers
holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt
the number of times a unit of currency changes hands in financing a year's output
the notes and coin held by the public plus the reserves banks keep with the central authority
items.s: Velocity of circulation: the number of times a unit of currency changes hands in financing a year's output. The other options describe Financial intermediation, High-powered money, Precautionary motive.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the part of a shortfall caused by weak activity rather than by deliberate choices”
o: Cyclical deficit
Debt monetisation
Debt sustainability
Structural deficit
items.s: Cyclical deficit is the part of a shortfall caused by weak activity rather than by deliberate choices.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Hysteresis.
o: a rise in the general price level that people foresaw and allowed for in their bargains
the loss of purchasing power that holders of cash suffer when the state prints money
a name for the jobless share below which price rises begin to accelerate
the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal
items.s: Hysteresis: the tendency for a long spell of joblessness to raise the level that afterwards counts as normal. The other options describe Inflation tax, NAIRU, Anticipated inflation.

items.q: The correct meaning of Demand shock is
o: the shortfall of spending that leaves output below its full-employment level
the total that firms will offer at each price level while some costs are held by past bargains
the difference between what the economy actually produces and what it could produce with its resources fully used
an unexpected change in spending plans that moves the total wanted at every price level
items.s: Demand shock: an unexpected change in spending plans that moves the total wanted at every price level. The other options describe Output gap, Short-run aggregate supply, Recessionary gap.

items.q: Supply shock may be defined as
o: the difference between what the economy actually produces and what it could produce with its resources fully used
the total that firms will offer at each price level while some costs are held by past bargains
a sudden change in the cost or availability of inputs that shifts what firms will offer at every price
the total amount of finished output that buyers at home and abroad wish to purchase at each price level
items.s: Supply shock: a sudden change in the cost or availability of inputs that shifts what firms will offer at every price. The other options describe Aggregate demand, Short-run aggregate supply, Output gap.

items.q: “the financing of a shortfall by creating money rather than by borrowing from the public” is the definition of
o: Debt monetisation
Ricardian equivalence
Fiscal federalism
Structural deficit
items.s: Debt monetisation is the financing of a shortfall by creating money rather than by borrowing from the public.

items.q: In this course, Purchasing power parity refers to
o: the holdings of other countries' money and gold that a state uses to defend its currency
the view that currencies should exchange so that a basket of items costs the same everywhere
a rise in a currency's value against others under market forces
a deliberate lowering of a currency's fixed value against others
items.s: Purchasing power parity: the view that currencies should exchange so that a basket of items costs the same everywhere. The other options describe Foreign reserves, Devaluation, Appreciation.

items.q: The correct meaning of Transmission mechanism is
o: the boost to spending when a fixed stock of cash buys more because prices have fallen
the chain by which a change in the policy interest works through credit and the currency to spending
the set of income and interest combinations at which spending plans and output are equal
the lift to private spending that public outlay can give when it improves conditions for business
items.s: Transmission mechanism: the chain by which a change in the policy interest works through credit and the currency to spending. The other options describe Real balance effect, Crowding-in, IS schedule.

items.q: The correct meaning of Precautionary motive is
o: holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt
the practice of refusing loans to some applicants at the going interest instead of raising the charge
the work of banks in taking funds from savers and lending them to borrowers
the proposition that a change in the stock of cash brings a proportionate change in prices when output is fixed
items.s: Precautionary motive: holding cash to meet unforeseen outlays that may arise before the next receipt. The other options describe Credit rationing, Financial intermediation, Quantity theory.
items.t: Money, credit and the financial system

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Real wage rigidity?
o: the divide between those already in work who bargain for pay and those outside who cannot
the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high
the time and effort spent looking for a suitable opening
the observed tendency for each extra point of joblessness to be matched by a fall in output relative to capacity
items.s: Real wage rigidity: the failure of pay to fall when conditions weaken, which keeps joblessness high. The other options describe Job search, Insider-outsider, Okun's law.

items.q: The correct meaning of LM schedule is
o: the boost to spending when a fixed stock of cash buys more because prices have fallen
the set of income and interest combinations at which the wish to hold cash equals the amount in circulation
the chain by which a change in the policy interest works through credit and the currency to spending
the combination of taxing, spending and interest measures used together
items.s: LM schedule: the set of income and interest combinations at which the wish to hold cash equals the amount in circulation. The other options describe Real balance effect, Transmission mechanism, Policy mix.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the shortfall of spending that leaves output below its full-employment level”
o: Recessionary gap
Output gap
Supply shock
Long-run aggregate supply
items.s: Recessionary gap is the shortfall of spending that leaves output below its full-employment level.

items.q: Policy rate may be defined as
o: a limit on how much banks may lend in total or to particular sectors
the interest a central authority charges when it lends to banks overnight
fixing or limiting the value of the currency against another as the anchor of policy
a framework in which the central authority announces a price goal and is judged on reaching it
items.s: Policy rate: the interest a central authority charges when it lends to banks overnight. The other options describe Inflation targeting, Credit ceiling, Exchange rate targeting.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the part of output growth not explained by more labour and equipment, reflecting better methods”
o: Demographic dividend
Steady state
Total factor productivity
Convergence
items.s: Total factor productivity is the part of output growth not explained by more labour and equipment, reflecting better methods.

items.q: In this course, Permanent income view refers to
o: the rise in prices that households expect, which inclines them to spend sooner and set aside less
the change in outlay that follows a change in the worth of the assets people hold
the idea that outlay rests on the means people expect to keep over the long term rather than this year's figure
the idea that people smooth their outlay across a lifetime, borrowing when young and drawing down when old
items.s: Permanent income view: the idea that outlay rests on the means people expect to keep over the long term rather than this year's figure. The other options describe Wealth effect, Inflationary expectations, Life-cycle view of saving.

items.q: “the set of income and interest combinations at which the wish to hold cash equals the amount in circulation” is the definition of
o: LM schedule
Crowding-in
Real balance effect
IS schedule
items.s: LM schedule is the set of income and interest combinations at which the wish to hold cash equals the amount in circulation.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the ratio of the change in income to the change in tax collection that brought it about”
o: Balanced-budget multiplier
Open-economy multiplier
Induced expenditure
Tax multiplier
items.s: Tax multiplier is the ratio of the change in income to the change in tax collection that brought it about.
items.t: The multiplier in an open economy

items.q: Three of these relate to Consumption, saving and investment. Which one does not?
o: Relative income view
Permanent income view
Policy mix
Life-cycle view of saving
items.s: Every other option belongs to Consumption, saving and investment. “Policy mix” belongs to Goods and money market balance, not Consumption, saving and investment.

items.q: In this course, Devaluation refers to
o: a deliberate lowering of a currency's fixed value against others
a rise in a currency's value against others under market forces
the requirement that combined import and export responsiveness exceed one before a weaker currency narrows the trade gap
the pattern in which a weaker currency worsens the trade gap before improving it
items.s: Devaluation: a deliberate lowering of a currency's fixed value against others. The other options describe J-curve, Marshall-Lerner condition, Appreciation.
